title: Grim Message
html:
Grim Message

When the characters say the stone's command phrase, its illusion activates and the characters see an image of Zulkir Thrul.

Read or paraphrase the following:

Magical energy shimmers, and a translucent image appears: Zulkir Thrul sits behind her desk, looking stern.

"If you're seeing this, operatives, it means I'm incapacitated or dead," she says. "But you aren't, and therefore Thay has hope. Know that I am proud of you—but your work is not yet done.

"The Hydra is ensconced in his stronghold in Thaymount—the Citadel—where he is nearly unassailable. Layered wards protect the area from teleportation and scrying, and by now every inch of it crawls with malefites and fiends. We have mere days before he finishes his ritual, raises his hordes, and declares himself regent again.

"Use the Mavericks' ritual to travel to central Thaymount. From there, find the underground tunnel that leads from Castle Thrul—my ancestral home—into the Citadel. You must reach the Citadel without delay.

"The Hydra knows about this underground passage, and his allies may have magically barricaded Castle Thrul to prevent entry. In this case, seek the advice of Sabinia Dau in the Veiled Tower. If she's unsure, you'll need the help of her sister, Saraphine, the most brilliant magical theorist I've known. She's most likely in Thaymount.

"I've left magic items in my demiplane that might aid you. Consider them payment."

The zulkir exhales, then smiles grimly, head held high. "You can save Thay from the Hydra, operatives. I believe in you."

Szass Tam's Barrier

As Zulkir Thrul suspects, Szass Tam has erected a powerful barrier around Castle Thrul as described in "Abyssal Barriers" later in this chapter.

Zulkir Thrul's Fate

Zulkir Thrul is alive—barely—because Szass Tam wants her to witness his ritual's completion before he turns her into an undead servant. Thaymount's wards against scrying (see "Magic on Thaymount" later in this chapter) prevent the characters from locating or magically observing Thrul, but they'll have a chance to reunite with her in chapter 7.

Zulkir Thrul's Demiplane

If the characters can cast Demiplane, they can enter Zulkir Thrul's demiplane. If they do so, they find it exactly as described in chapter 3, except the following are neatly laid on the zulkir's desk:

  • Animated Shield
  • Plate Armor of Etherealness
  • Potion of Greater Healing
  • Robe of the Archmagi
  • Spellguard Shield
  • Staff of the Magi
  • Vorpal Greatsword
The zulkir's payment includes Potion of Greater Healing.

If she's unsure, you'll need the help of her sister, Saraphine, the most brilliant magical theorist I've known. She's most likely in Thaymount.

"I've left magic items in my demiplane that might aid you. Consider them payment."

The zulkir exhales, then smiles grimly, head held high. "You can save Thay from the Hydra, operatives. I believe in you."

title: The zulkir's payment includes Potion of Greater Healing.
Reaching Thaymount
html:
Reaching Thaymount

The characters might debate traveling to Thaymount via teleportation to Szul—the only place in the region not warded against teleportation. Make it clear that doing so would be a death sentence, as Szass Tam has stationed an overwhelming force here that the characters can't overcome. They must rely on the Mavericks' ritual to teleport to a location in central Thaymount.

The characters' options for getting there depend on the outcome of their mission to recruit the Mavericks in chapter 5.

The Mavericks Assist

If the characters allied with the dissident Red Wizards, they can return to the Veiled Tower to obtain the mages' assistance with reaching Thaymount.

When the characters enter the tower, read or paraphrase the following:

In the tower's lounge, scattered notes, open books, and strange spell components cover the table. Before you stand the five dissident Red Wizards, looking weary. Darvyn Yev greets you.

"As promised, we have finished the ritual to teleport to central Thaymount. Given the situation, though, we have some concerns that you can help with."

Speaking with Yev

Yev reveals the following in conversation:

  • The Mavericks' Fears. Yev explains condescendingly that the mages fear that Szass Tam's evil magic and marauding allies have made central Thaymount unsafe.
  • A Coward's Proposal. Yev suggests that the Red Wizards teleport the characters to the Mouth of Despair (as described in chapter 5), while the Red Wizards stay in the Veiled Tower until the party tells them the Fortress of Opposition is safe.

Speaking with Sabinia Dau

If the characters ask Sabinia Dau about circumventing the barrier around Castle Thrul, she ponders their question carefully. Read or paraphrase the following:

"If Szass Tam is trying to prevent you from entering Castle Thrul, you won't be able to circumvent his barrier with everyday magic," Dau says.

"I doubt I could help even if I knew the details. However, my sister Saraphine is a genius when it comes to magical barriers. She'll know how to thwart it—and she's likely to have the magic on hand. Saraphine's in Thaymount, in our family's home, the Fortress of Opposition."

Dau's Request

Regardless whether the characters ask about traveling to Castle Thrul, before the mages begin the ritual, Dau asks them to investigate the Fortress of Opposition and confirm Saraphine's safety.

If the characters agree, Dau gives them the perfumes, rare oils, and coins (worth 40,000 GP in total) and the Crystal Ball of Ominous Portent (see appendix A) that she keeps in her bedroom (area V5d on map 5.1 in chapter 5).

Saraphine, a human, was residing at the fortress with five others when Szass Tam began his final ritual steps and Thaymount was thrown into chaos (see "Thaymount in Chaos" later in this chapter). More information about the fortress's inhabitants appears in "Trapped Inhabitants" later in this chapter.

Performing the Teleportation Ritual

When the characters are ready, the Red Wizards perform their ritual, which takes 10 minutes. Afterward, the characters arrive in the Mouth of Despair (see "Central Thaymount").

The Mavericks Don't Assist

If the characters failed to impress the dissident Red Wizards—or killed them—they can still use the mages' ritual to reach Thaymount.

The Mavericks Are Dead

If the dissidents died, the characters can use the ritual notes and components in Darvyn Yev's bedroom (area V5e on map 5.1 in chapter 5) to teleport to central Thaymount. However, the unfinished ritual proves difficult to perform.

The characters each must take an action to follow the notes and make a 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a success, a character teleports to central Thaymount and takes 22 (5d8) Force damage. On a failure, a character teleports there and takes 45 (10d8) Force damage.

The Mavericks Are Unimpressed

If the characters failed to impress the dissidents in chapter 5, they can return to the Veiled Tower and ask for the mages' help again.

A character must take the Influence action to explain what has happened since their last meeting with the mages, then make a 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check. On a success, the mages explain that they've finished the ritual to teleport to Thaymount and agree to help the characters. Proceed with "Speaking with Yev" above.

On a failure, the mages are enraged at the characters' incompetence and fight them. When one mage is Bloodied, however, the Mavericks reassess the characters' abilities, stop fighting, and tell the characters they've finished their ritual to travel to Thaymount. Proceed with "Speaking with Yev" above.

title: Central Thaymount
html:
Central Thaymount

When the characters teleport to central Thaymount, an area many miles across, they arrive in the Mouth of Despair, as shown on map 6.1. See "Thaymount" in chapter 1 for details on the tharch.

Mouth of Despair

A natural fissure in the plateau, the Mouth of Despair divides the Fortress of Opposition, Castle Thrul, and the Citadel from the more populated areas to the west.

The dissident Red Wizards targeted this area to avoid Szass Tam knowing about their arrival in Thaymount. Now that the characters are involved, these mages are happy to let the characters face Thaymount's dangers and report back.

The Red Wizards' ritual deposits the characters in the middle of the Mouth of Despair, at the bottom of the fissure near its eastern wall. When they arrive, read or paraphrase the following:

You find yourselves at the bottom of a forty-foot-deep chasm. Above, green lightning flashes amid a gray, oppressive haze pierced only by Thaymount's volcanic peaks far overhead.

Dim Light filters into the chasm during daytime.

Before the characters leave the Mouth of Despair, they see an illusion of Saraphine Dau, as described below.

Saraphine's Plea

If the characters reached the Mouth of Despair with the help of the dissident Red Wizards, Sabinia Dau told her sister via a Spell Scroll of Sending where and when to expect the characters to arrive in Central Thaymount. Shortly afterward, demons began attacking the Fortress of Opposition. Saraphine hid in the fortress and, desperate for help, used a Spell Scroll of Project Image to create an illusory copy of herself, which she sent into the Mouth of Despair to meet the characters.

If the dissident Red Wizards are dead, Saraphine sent her illusory copy here knowing that the mages were working on a way to reach the Mouth of Despair. It's a long shot, but she hopes her sister will arrive in the fissure and help her escape the fortress.

Read or paraphrase the following, changing Saraphine's recognition to surprise if she isn't expecting the characters to arrive:

Sitting on a nearby rock outcropping is the shimmering image of a young human woman, her navy blue cloak drawn around her. When she notices you, relief and excitement cross her face.

"You must be Sabinia's friends!" she says. "I'm Saraphine Dau, Sabinia's sister. You've got to help me! I'm stuck in the Fortress of Opposition. Fiends are destroying the place, and I fear they'll soon rip me to pieces. Others are hiding in the fortress too. Please help us!"

The characters recognize the image as an illusion. Saraphine Dau's image offers the characters the scrolls and magic items she keeps in the fortress (see area F14) in exchange for saving her and the others trapped in the fortress. She can tell the characters everything in the "Trapped Inhabitants" section.

If the characters ask Saraphine about the barrier around Castle Thrul, she won't discuss the matter until the characters agree to help her.

Magic on Thaymount

Ancient magical wards erected by paranoid Red Wizards block scrying and teleportation in most of Thaymount. The exception is Szul, one of Szass Tam's strongholds (see chapter 1).

Spells and effects that would teleport creatures to other areas of Thaymount don't work. In addition, the following spells don't function in Thaymount:

  • Arcane Eye
  • Beast Sense
  • Clairvoyance
  • Locate Creature
  • Locate Object
  • Passwall
  • Scrying

If a creature tries to cast one of these spells, the spell slot is expended, but the spell has no effect.

Creatures with Legendary Actions that are in their lairs (such as Szass Tam in chapter 7) ignore these impediments and can teleport or cast spells normally.

Thaymount in Chaos

With Szass Tam's ritual animating malefites and allowing demons to slip onto the Material Plane, Thaymount is in chaos. Central Thaymount is sparsely inhabited, though Castle Thrul and the Fortress of Opposition are both under attack, and magical barriers surround Castle Thrul and the Citadel (see "Abyssal Barriers"). Central Thaymount's layout is shown on map 6.1.

Malefites and demons have overrun this area. Every mile the adventurers spend traveling, roll once on the Thaymount Encounters table below. As shown on map 6.1, the Mouth of Despair is about seven miles from the Fortress of Opposition, which is about eight miles from Castle Thrul.

Use map 4.1 in chapter 4 for each encounter, but clarify to the players that its location is Thaymount.

Thaymount Encounters
1d4Encounter
1A Death Knight directs four Hezrou to dig in the rocky soil of an ancient graveyard. The demons search for dead spellcasters who will animate once Szass Tam completes his ritual.
2A Balor guarded by three Death Cultist tries to open a portal to the Abyss. Nearby are the corpses of a dozen Red Wizards who tried to stop them.
3A Marilith and three Death Knight Aspirant hunt for vulnerable people to slaughter.
4Two Goristro make their way west to attack mages' fortresses nearby.

Rising Evil Magic

As in Eltabbar, Szass Tam's demonic magic has created an ominous haze over Thaymount. Outdoor areas are in Dim Light in the daytime, and green lightning flashes in the sky.

Abyssal Barriers

When Szass Tam discovered Operation Deadfall, he used Abyssal magic to erect powerful barriers around Castle Thrul and the Citadel. The barriers are shown on map 6.1 and look like thick, green, translucent domes.

Castle Thrul

A barrier surrounds Castle Thrul outside the crumbling stone walls that surround the complex. The barrier functions like a Wall of Force spell, but it's permanent and can't be destroyed with a Disintegrate spell. The barrier prevents entry into the areas described in "Castle Thrul" later in this chapter. The characters can punch a hole in this barrier using Saraphine Dau's instructions (see area F14 in "Fortress of Opposition").

The Citadel

Another domed barrier surrounds the Citadel. It functions like the barrier surrounding Castle Thrul, but it can't be penetrated. However, the barrier doesn't extend far enough underground to impede the characters from reaching Szass Tam's ritual chamber via the tunnels under Castle Thrul.

The ritual's foul magic bathes the Citadel in green, malevolent energy that sweeps east, as shown on map 6.1. This energy is harmless to the living, but if Szass Tam's ritual isn't stopped, the energy will envelop Thaymount, causing malefites to rise en masse.

title: Fortress of Opposition
html:
Fortress of Opposition

The Fortress of Opposition comprises two structures that form one facility. The eastern portion stands atop a sixty-foot cliff, while the western portion sits at the cliff's base. A staircase connects the two sections.

The Dau family of Red Wizards has owned the fortress for centuries. While most family members prefer primary residences in more cosmopolitan parts of Thay, Saraphine Dau relishes the fortress's isolation. It's her primary residence. (For more about Saraphine, see "Trapped Inhabitants" below.)

Read or paraphrase the following when the characters approach the Fortress of Opposition:

A sturdy fortress rises before you in two sections: a broad structure with a central tower and numerous small towers around its perimeter, and a wide tower atop a sixty-foot cliff to the east connected to the structure below. Green lightning strikes the upper portion, while hulking demonic forms lumber near the lower towers.

Trapped Inhabitants

Saraphine Dau, her friend, and two Dau family staff are trapped inside the fortress. They were staying in the fortress when Szass Tam began escalating his ritual. When rampaging demons attacked the fortress, the staff and Saraphine's friend locked themselves in their bedrooms, while Saraphine, who was in the lab upstairs, locked herself inside and ordered the fortress's two guards to ward the lab's entrance.

The three hiding downstairs know each others' locations; they also know Saraphine was in the lab and the two guards were in the fortress's lounge, but they don't know that the guards have been killed or whether Saraphine is alive. Similarly, Saraphine is unaware of the fate of those downstairs.

The names and locations of these individuals are in the Trapped Inhabitants table below.

Trapped Inhabitants
NameArea Found
AventrilF3
Jerica ReyF5
Molly MaluF4
Saraphine DauF14

Rescuing the Inhabitants

If the characters defeat the monsters in the fortress courtyard (area F1), great hall (area F2), and library (area F8), and tell those trapped in the bedchambers (areas F3–F5) that they did so, those three inhabitants become Friendly [Attitude] toward the party and unlock their doors. If the characters haven't rescued Saraphine in the lab (area F14), those downstairs beg the characters to rescue her before they'll talk further. Otherwise, they thank the characters profusely and offer to help the characters in any way they can, including giving them any treasure they have. See area F14 for Saraphine's response to rescue.

If the characters don't defeat all the creatures in the fortress, the besieging forces break through the locked doors—or smash holes in the walls—in one hour and kill Saraphine and the others.

Assaulting Force

When Sabinia Dau published her anti-Szass Tam pamphlet, "Death to Tyrants," the dragonborn Goreth Blacktooth took note. A low-ranking officer in Szass Tam's Dread Legion (see chapter 1), Blacktooth recently mustered two undead knights and set off for the Fortress of Opposition, hoping to earn a position closer to Szass Tam's side by killing Sabinia Dau, who he assumes is in the fortress.

Blacktooth has marshaled demons and undead he encountered en route to attack the fortress. They are only loosely under his command and are mostly interested in causing destruction and suffering.

Fortress Features

The fortress is made of magically treated stone that has Resistance to all damage. The structure also has the following features.

Ceilings

Ceilings in the fortress are 50 feet high, except for the ceiling over the staircase leading from area F2

Doors

The fortress's doors are made of magically treated metal that has Resistance to all damage. The doors to most bedrooms (areas F3–F6) are locked; their locks are Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality (20). (See "Doors" in the Dungeon Master's Guide.)

Lighting

Sconces with Continual Flame spells cast on them shed Bright Light in all interior areas. Outside, the evil magic haze swirling in the region allows only Dim Light to shine through during the day.

Thaymount's Wards

Like everywhere on the plateau, the fortress is affected by Thaymount's ancient magical wards (see "Magic on Thaymount" earlier in this chapter).

Fortress Locations

The following locations are keyed to map 6.2.

F1: Fortress Courtyard

The fortress's enormous metal doors lie shattered on the ground. A massive fiend resembling a nightmarish centaur slams a warhammer against the northwest wall, while two horned, toad-faced monsters drool and laugh evilly. Meanwhile, skeletons and zombies claw ineffectually at the fortress's outer wall.

A Rendelith (see appendix B) works to smash its way into a bedchamber inside the fortress (area F3) while two Hezrou rumble encouragement. The demons fight the characters as soon as they notice them.

Five groups of undead (each made up of five Skeleton and five Zombie) scrabble at different sections of the outer wall, to no effect.

F2: Great Hall

Ripped carpets and smashed furniture litter this once-luxurious hall with soaring ceilings. A staircase in the northeast corner spirals upward.

Two fiendish horrors lumber purposefully toward the northwest: massive, horned creatures with black, bony spikes protruding from their crimson-furred backs. Elsewhere in the hall, skeletons and zombies shamble aimlessly.

The Fiends are two Goristro, which are searching for the inhabitants who have locked themselves in nearby bedchambers (areas F3–F5). The goristros fight the characters as soon as they notice them.

Lying in wait to the north of the library (area F8), out of sight of the entrance, is an Abveku (see appendix B). It joins the fight when the goristros begin combat. Four groups of undead, each made up of five Skeleton and five Zombie, scrabble at the doors that lead to bedchambers.

F3: South Bedchamber

The door to this room is locked as detailed in "Fortress Features."

A bed, nightstand, and wardrobe furnish this comfortable bedroom, and its textiles boast subtle patterns. A human man wearing a green-and-gold robe huddles on the bed.

Hiding here is Aventril (Medium Noble), a personal assistant to Saraphine. A no-nonsense but friendly human man, Aventril manages Saraphine's calendar and stays here while Saraphine is in residence.

Treasure

Aventril has few valuable personal possessions, but he does keep a Potion of Gaseous Form and a Potion of Comprehension in his nightstand.

F4: Southwest Bedchamber

The door to this room is locked as detailed in "Fortress Features."

This comfortable bedroom is decorated in geometric patterns. A bed, wardrobe, and nightstand furnish the room. A human woman with waist-length black hair paces the floor.

Hiding here is Molly Malu (Medium Noble), a personal assistant to Saraphine. The bubbly and passionate human woman provides Saraphine with social advice and organizes the parties Saraphine throws in Eltabbar.

Treasure

Malu enjoys fashion. Fifteen sets of Fine Clothes hang in her wardrobe.

F5: North Bedchamber

The door to this room is locked as detailed in "Fortress Features."

This bedroom is decorated with velvet curtains and bedclothes, a silk rug, and stylized wood carvings. It's furnished with a bed, a nightstand, and a wardrobe. A young, pale gnome woman sits on the bed scribbling notes in a journal.

Jerica Rey (Small Mage Apprentice), Saraphine's close friend and fellow aspiring Red Wizard, hides here. The young gnome hasn't yet earned an apprenticeship with a Red Wizard, though it's her ardent wish. Rey is chronicling her ordeal in her journal when the characters arrive.

Treasure

Rey wears a Cloak of Displacement but gripes about not having other magic items. She tells the characters about the repository of Spell Scroll and magic items in the magical lab (area F14).

F6: Northeast Bedchamber

The door to this room is locked as detailed in "Fortress Features."

In this comfortable bedroom, Red Wizard symbols adorn the duvet and rug. Sitting on the nightstand are a stoppered flask and a clay jug.

Sabinia Dau stays here when she visits.

Treasure

On the nightstand are an Alchemy Jug and a Decanter of Endless Water.

F7: Southeast Bedchamber

This bedroom lies in shambles. The door hangs open on its hinges. Someone has snapped the wooden bed frame, torn the rugs, and splintered the wardrobe and nightstand.

Normally the guards' bedroom, this chamber was destroyed by the Goristro in the great hall (area F2).

F8: Library

Two enormous, board-headed beasts knock over bookshelves in this spacious library while a six-armed, serpentine fiend flings tables and scatters books around the room.

Two Nalfeshnee and a Marilith wreak havoc here. They fight the characters as soon as they notice them.

Treasure

If the characters spend 10 minutes searching the toppled shelves, they find a Spell Scroll of Circle of Power and a Spell Scroll of Contact Other Plane among the wreckage.

F9: Azuth Shrine

A fifteen-foot-tall pyramid made of gold sits in this room's west alcove. Around it flit colored lights. A symbol emblazoned near the pyramid's apex depicts a hand holding up its index finger.

This room is a shrine to Azuth, god of spellcasting, whom the Dau family worships. Any character who has proficiency in Religion or worships Azuth recognizes the symbol.

Praying at the Shrine

Azuth, the Lord of Spells, is aware of the events unfolding and wants the characters to stop Szass Tam. If a creature takes an action to pray at the shrine, Azuth restores that creature's expended spell slots. A creature can benefit from the shrine only once every 24 hours.

F10: Abyssal Vestibule

A double door stands in the east wall here, and a spiral staircase leads down in its north end. A mirror and furniture lie smashed on the floor.

Scorched red banners bearing a pronged symbol hang in ripped ribbons from the hundred-foot ceiling. The portraits of red-robed mages that adorn the curved walls bear smears of filth and claw marks.

The mages in the paintings suddenly grow horns, and their eyes glow green. They try to scrabble out of the walls, hissing like demonic beasts, and an overwhelming sense of murderous chaos washes over you.

A Marilith desecrated this place with Abyssal filth it brought when it slipped onto the Material Plane. Blacktooth and his death knights then urged it to proceed to the lounge (see area F11).

Demonic Possession

When a character enters this area, they can take the Study action to focus on the portraits' unsettling images and make a 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a success, the character realizes the portraits' movements aren't real and that the area is desecrated with Abyssal energy. The character knows that any player character who lingers in this room for 1 minute or longer will be subject to possession by demons.

If a character lingers in the room for 1 minute or longer, the character hears the mages speak with demonic voices. The mages say phrases in Abyssal such as "Bathe in their blood!" and "Chaos and murder reign supreme." The character is the target of Demonic Possession, as described in the Dungeon Master's Guide. A character is targeted by this effect only once.

F11: Lounge

What was once a beautiful lounge lies in disarray. Armchairs are toppled, and tables are smashed. Two bodies, blood dried on their dented plate armor, lie splayed on the floor. A hulking dragonborn man in black armor watches while a six-armed monster and two desiccated, black-armored knights with green, glowing eyes move to attack a double door to the northeast.

A Marilith and two Death Knight Aspirant move to assault the locked doors to area F14 as Goreth Blacktooth (Medium, Neutral Evil Warrior Commander) looks on. When any of them notices the characters, they fight to the death; Goreth shrieks his devotion to Szass Tam all the while.

Bodies

The bodies are those of Dau family guards: the orc Gregesh and the human Karla. Saraphine asked them to guard the doors to the magical lab (area F14); Goreth and his allies slaughtered them before the characters arrived.

Treasure

A +1 Greatsword lies near the western fallen guard.

F12: Study

This cozy space boasts comfortable chairs, a table, and many open books.

Saraphine was pouring through tomes here before Goreth Blacktooth attacked the fortress.

Treasure

If the characters spend 10 minutes searching this room, they find a Tome of Leadership and Influence among the books.

F13: Armory

Suits of armor are stored here, and weapon racks stand against the east wall.

Weapons and armor are kept here for use by the family's guards.

Treasure

The armor stands and weapon racks hold the following items:

  • Two Longsword
  • Three Spear
  • Plate Armor
  • Scale Mail

F14: Magical Lab

The double door to this area is locked with an Arcane Lock spell. When the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

An enormous desk curves along the south and east walls, supporting magical laboratory equipment. At the desk, a young human woman frantically scans a book and mumbles to herself. Shelves stand against the north and west walls.

The characters recognize the woman as Saraphine Dau (Medium Mage), Sabinia's sister.

Saraphine is overjoyed if the characters have killed the monsters in the fortress. If they haven't yet freed the people trapped in the bedchambers (areas F3–F5), she begs the characters to do so. She feels terrible that the assault on the fortress began before she could usher the others into the safety of this lab and that the guards died trying to defend her.

Here, generations of the Dau family have researched magic and created new spells. Although she's not yet a Red Wizard, Saraphine covets the title and hopes to make magical advances to impress the mages and her family. She is an ingenious magical researcher and understands magical theory better than most Red Wizards, though she finds spellcasting difficult.

Development

If the characters defeat all the monsters in the Fortress of Opposition, Saraphine gladly answers their questions about magical barriers. When the characters describe the barrier around Castle Thrul, read or paraphrase the following:

Saraphine sighs thoughtfully, then snaps her fingers in triumph.

"Yes, of course!" she exclaims. "The barrier must be constructed from Abyssal energy. It's like a wall of force but more potent. You need disintegration magic designed specifically to affect the spiritual resonances of that realm.

"I've got a scroll I can make some adjustments to. You can use it to punch a hole in the barrier."

Saraphine rummages through a nearby table and finds a Spell Scroll of Disintegrate. Over the course of 10 minutes, she makes adjustments to the scroll's writing and diagrams. She then offers the modified scroll to the characters.

Saraphine explains that a character must use the adjusted Spell Scroll while within 30 feet of the barrier around Castle Thrul. Doing this will create a permanent 10-foot-by-10-foot hole in the barrier.

If no character can use the scroll, Saraphine instead scribbles a phonetic representation of the Disintegrate spell's modified verbal component. She modifies and then demonstrates the accompanying somatic component. She tells the characters that one of them must re-create these components within 30 feet of the barrier to create a permanent 10-foot-by-10-foot hole in it. This is dangerous; see "Abyssal Barrier" in "Castle Thrul."

Once the fortress is free of monsters, Saraphine musters the other trapped inhabitants to stay in the lab with her until the region is safe.

When the characters learn how to punch a hole in the barrier around Castle Thrul, each character earns 11,700 XP.

Treasure

Saraphine gives the characters the items she has stockpiled here to help their fight against Szass Tam:

  • Potion of Heroism
  • Three Potion of Superior Healing
  • Ring of Candor (see appendix A)
  • Spell Scroll of Antimagic Field
  • Spell Scroll of Stoneskin
  • Spell Scroll of True Seeing
  • Two Spell Scroll of Project Image

F15: Storage

Shelves full of linens and open boxes line the walls of this storage room.

This room holds household supplies.

Treasure

If the characters search this room, they find three vials each of Acid, Alchemist's Fire, Antitoxin, and Basic Poison.

F16: Master Bedchamber

Within this luxurious room, a gorgeous canopy bed with embroidered silk hangings occupies the northeast corner, an ornate wardrobe sits along the southwest wall, and an armchair nestles into the northwest corner.

This is Saraphine's bedroom.

Treasure

Twenty sets of Fine Clothes hang in the wardrobe. A drawer inside the wardrobe holds five diamonds worth 25,000 GP total.

title: Castle Thrul
html:
Castle Thrul

One of the oldest buildings in Thaymount, Castle Thrul is a sprawling stone complex that includes a main hall and a 130-foot central tower surrounded by a stone wall. A necropolis where esteemed family members are interred sits south of the primary complex. An underground tunnel in the necropolis's largest mausoleum leads into the castle's armory (area C8 on map 6.3), while a passage in the northeast wing (area C13) leads to the Citadel, where Szass Tam weaves his ritual.

Lich's Strike Force

When Szass Tam discovered Zulkir Thrul was behind Operation Deadfall, he vowed to destroy her and everyone she loves, starting with those in Castle Thrul. The lich assigned this job to the demilich Yoreth, whose lair is in the Citadel, and the human Red Wizard Jarek.

Szass Tam instructed Yoreth and Jarek to marshal demonic and undead forces to descend on Castle Thrul and kill anyone they encountered.

Keeping the Characters Out

After Szass Tam dispatched Yoreth and Jarek to Castle Thrul, the lich erected a barrier around the castle grounds outside the stone wall as described in "Abyssal Barriers" earlier in this chapter.

As a contingency, Szass Tam instructed Yoreth to set a trap for the characters.

False Zulkir

Using a Spell Scroll of Programmed Illusion (17), Jarek has created an illusion of Zulkir Thrul bound with magically glowing chains to the summit of the castle's tower (area C15). The illusion activates when the characters come within 150 feet of the castle. For five minutes, the illusion depicts Thrul struggling against the chains and shouting for help. After five minutes, it disappears; it reactivates after 10 minutes if the party moves anywhere outside the castle within 150 feet.

Jarek hopes the illusion will fool the characters into trying to rescue the zulkir so Jarek, Yoreth, and their balor ally can ambush them.

Approaching the Castle

Read or paraphrase the following when the characters come within 150 feet of Castle Thrul:

Black haze billows in the sky, where green lightning flashes. Behind a translucent green barrier, a stalwart fortress ringed by a stone wall rises along the hill before you. South of the fortress, squat buildings with interspersed gravestones stands somberly; four black-armored soldiers patrol the grounds with jerky movements.

Jutting from the fortress against the hazy horizon is a tower, around which flies a tiny orb that glows green. Lashed to the tower is a red-robed figure that shouts for help.

Castle Features

Castle Thrul is made of magically treated stone that has Resistance to all damage. The castle otherwise has the following features.

Abyssal Barrier

The characters must punch a hole through the Abyssal barrier surrounding the castle (see area F14 in "Fortress of Opposition" earlier in this chapter). They can create this hole anywhere they want.

If the characters use Saraphine's modified verbal and somatic components to punch a hole in the barrier instead of her modified Spell Scroll of Disintegrate, a character takes an action to follow Saraphine's instructions and makes a 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a successful check, the character punches a hole in the barrier and takes 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage from magical backlash. On a failure, the character punches a hole in the barrier, but the magical backlash rips through them, and they take 27 (6d8) Necrotic damage.

Ceilings

Ceilings in buildings in the necropolis (area C1) are 10 feet high. The ceiling in the guard tower (area C2) is 20 feet high. Those on the castle's main floor (areas C4–C14) are 30 feet high.

Corpses

Yoreth and Jarek's forces killed many of those who were in Castle Thrul when their strike force descended. Bodies of these victims are in areas C2–C4. The victims knew key information that can help the characters as they explore the castle.

The characters might communicate with or raise a victim from the dead, perhaps using the Rod of Resurrection found in area C1 to cast Resurrection on a victim. Each victim shares a different piece of information, beginning with "Door Passphrase," until the characters know all the following:

  • Door Passphrase. The only way to open the door to the gallery (area C10) is to use the passphrase "Thay shall endure."
  • Lurking Balor. The forces that are attacking the castle include a balor.
  • Strike Force Leaders. The forces that overran the castle were led by a demilich named Yoreth and a Red Wizard named Jarek, both of whom serve Szass Tam.
  • Tower Trap. The leaders of the attack on the castle bragged about a trap involving an illusion of Zulkir Thrul lashed to the tower (area C15).

Doors

The castle's doors are made of metal and are unlocked, except for the double door leading into the gallery (area C10).

Lighting

Areas outside Castle Thrul have Dim Light during the day due to the evil magic that swirls through Thaymount. Inside the castle, sconces with Continual Flame spells cast on them shed Bright Light.

Structural Damage

Castle Thrul has been under assault for days, during which time demons have damaged its structure—particularly the roof and walls on the west side of the fortress. The chunks of rubble on the ground in most of the western spaces (areas C6–C9) make those areas Difficult Terrain.

Thaymount's Wards

Like everywhere on the plateau, the castle is affected by Thaymount's ancient magical wards (see "Magic on Thaymount" earlier in this chapter).

Castle Locations

The following locations are keyed to map 6.3.

C1: Necropolis

A side path branching off the road to Castle Thrul leads to an austere graveyard at the base of a low cliff. The gravestones, obelisks, and covered tombs bear the names of Thrul ancestors.

A mausoleum sits on the necropolis's north end. Four soldiers in black armor with green, glowing eyes patrol the area haltingly.

The patrolling soldiers are four Death Knight Aspirant; they fight the characters on sight.

Graves

All the graves, some as old as four hundred years, belong to members of the Thrul family.

Mausoleum

The mausoleum includes four sarcophagi, in which are interred prominent Thrul Red Wizards. The mausoleum includes a shrine for offerings and a secret door to a tunnel leading into the castle (see below for both).

Secret Door

The back of the mausoleum houses a secret door (marked with an S on the map; 20 to notice), behind which a staircase leads to an underground tunnel. The tunnel leads to the armory (area C8). The door leading to area C8 is visible from inside the tunnel.

Treasure

An unlocked drawer in the shrine's base contains a Rod of Resurrection. On the shrine, jewelry worth 10,000 GP in total is laid out as offerings.

C2: Guard Tower

A stone tower sits at the castle complex's southwest corner. Inside slumps an armored body, whose sword lies nearby. A ladder leads upward.

The death knights in the necropolis (area C1) have already swept through this area.

Ladder

The ladder leads to the top of the guard tower, where battlements surround the flat roof. Any creature on the roof has Cover from creatures on the ground.

Thuvia's Corpse

The corpse belongs to Thuvia, captain of the Thruls' family guard. The rest of the guards fled the castle when Thuvia fell. See "Castle Features" for additional details on corpses.

Journal

Thuvia's small, leather-bound journal is tucked in a pouch on her belt. If the characters spend 10 minutes perusing it, they learn the passphrase to the locked door that leads to the gallery (area C10): "Thay shall endure."

Treasure

Thuvia's equipment includes a suit of Plate Armor and a +3 Longsword.

C3: Courtyard

Just west of the necropolis is a courtyard that holds a small well.

A peaked wooden roof tops the 5-foot-diameter stone well, which is 20 feet deep. The rope for the well's bucket has been cut, and the bucket has fallen into the well.

Xelnius's Corpse

In the well is the corpse of the human Red Wizard Xelnius Thrul, Zulkir Thrul's brother. Xelnius's body floats at the water's surface, 10 feet belowground, though it is easy to spot thanks to his red robes. Before he died, Xelnius was terrified for his sister, whom he loves dearly. See "Castle Features" for additional details on corpses.

Treasure

Xelnius wears a Headband of Intellect and a set of crimson Fine Clothes.

C4: Great Hall

A huge portcullis, ripped from its housing, lies dented here on the ground. Three enormous, crimson bipedal fiends with horns and massive claws rampage through the once-lavish great hall, knocking over pedestals, smashing busts and statues, and shredding crimson banners. Four armored bodies, their corpses twisted strangely, lie scattered about the room. A dais to the east leads to a large double door.

The fiends are three Goristro; they fight the characters on sight.

The hall was once decorated with tapestries and statuary depicting the glories of House Thrul over the centuries, but they've all been destroyed.

Corpses

The bodies are those of four Thrul family guards: the humans Retha and Rian and the orcs Wythe and Cadeth. See "Castle Features" for additional details on corpses.

Treasure

The guards' weapons and armor include the following:

  • Greatsword
  • Three Heavy Crossbow
  • Longbow
  • Six Longsword
  • Sap
  • Three Chain Shirt
  • Scale Mail
  • +3 Longsword

C5: North Library

Undisturbed bookshelves fill this small library.

The demons haven't reached this area yet.

Treasure

If the characters spend 10 minutes searching the shelves, they find a Tome of Clear Thought and a Tome of Understanding.

C6: South Library

Chunks of masonry have fallen from the roof here and lie atop collapsed shelves. Fallen books are scattered about the area.

Demons smashed a hole through the roof, showering the room with masonry.

Treasure

A character can take the Search action to sift through the rubble and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. On a success, the character finds a Manual of Golems.

C7: Mustering Yard

The south end of this open yard is choked with rubble from a partially collapsed wall.

This yard is abandoned.

C8: Armory

Weapons and shields litter the floor, and suits of armor lie strewn about. Rubble from the damaged ceiling fills the northwest corner.

This chamber stored arms and armor for the Thrul family's guards, as well as household supplies. Demons damaged the roof and tore through the armory, leaving it in disarray.

Secret Door

A secret door (marked with an S on the map; 20 to notice) opens to a steep staircase down. The stairs lead to a tunnel that emerges in the mausoleum in the necropolis (area C1). The secret door to the necropolis is visible from inside the tunnel.

Treasure

The Thrul family generously outfitted the castle's guards. A character who searches the area finds the following:

  • Two Greatsword
  • Two Longsword
  • Plate Armor
  • Three Scale Mail

C9: Barrack

Partial walls create a semblance of privacy in this crowded barrack. Rubble from a collapsed wall fills the southern half of the barrack.

This barrack once housed Thrul family guards and servants, as well as staff accompanying dignitaries. The servants were sent away when the situation in Thaymount escalated.

Treasure

As a Search action, a character can look under the beds and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. On a success, the character finds rucksacks under three of the beds. The rucksacks each contain various coins worth 250 GP total.

C10: Gallery

When the characters approach the gallery's entrance, read or paraphrase the following:

This metal double door bears embossed images of eight mages in regal poses and flowing robes. Most are bald and bear tattoos. Above the image are the words "All Glory to Thrul" in Common.

This double door is protected with a magical, Invisible barrier similar to the effect of a Wall of Force spell, except it can't be suppressed and a Disintegrate spell doesn't destroy it. Only speaking the passphrase "Thay shall endure" removes the barrier. The barrier reappears 1 minute after the passphrase is spoken.

A character can take the Study action to examine the barrier and make a 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a success, the character realizes a passphrase is the only way to bypass the barrier.

Discovering the Passphrase

The characters might learn the passphrase from one of the corpses in areas C2–C4 (see "Castle Features" for more about learning from corpses). They might also learn the passphrase from the journal on Thuvia's body in area C2.

Once the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

Eight twenty-foot-tall portraits of mages in crimson robes ring this gallery. Each portrait bears a brass nameplate. The portraits overlook a cozy, undisturbed lounge, with plush armchairs in the center and a spiral staircase to the north.

The eight nameplates bear the names Renia Thrul, Darius Thrul, Zulkir Aznar Thrul, Ferene Thrul, Xander Thrul, Vernus Thrul, Geryn Thrul, and Zulkir Xelnene Thrul. The characters recognize the portrait of Xelnene, who bears a dour, regal expression matching those of her ancestors.

If the characters aren't already aware of Zulkir Aznar Thrul, a character can take the Study action to examine Aznar's portrait and make a 15 Intelligence (History) check. On a success, the character knows everything in the "History" section of Xelnene Thrul's entry in appendix B.

Staircase

The staircase to the north ascends 130 feet to the top of the castle's tower (area C15).

C11: Thuvia's Chamber

This bedchamber displays an array of military medals. Along the south wall are two trunks.

This was the bedroom of guard captain Thuvia, whose body is in the guard tower (area C2). The Thruls considered her a member of the family.

Treasure

The left trunk holds Thuvia's emergency stash of coins. It totals 50,000 GP.

The trunk on the right contains five sets of Traveler's Clothes and a Dread Helm that was a gift from Xelnene Thrul's late father, Geryn.

C12: Xelnius's Chamber

This lavish chamber includes a bed with a blue duvet, a marble washbasin in a wooden stand, and two trunks to the north.

This was the bedroom of Xelnius Thrul, whose body was thrown into the well (area C3).

Treasure

The trunks and wardrobe are unlocked. The wardrobe holds ten sets of Fine Clothes. The right trunk contains four Potion of Superior Healing; the left one is empty.

C13: Zulkir Thrul's Chamber

This bedroom's red bedspread and nightstand bear a light layer of dust. A trapdoor is built into the stone floor.

This chamber is Xelnene Thrul's bedroom, though the zulkir rarely stays here. She keeps nothing of value in this room.

Underground Passage

The trapdoor on the south end of the room leads to a maze of tunnels underneath Thaymount. From this maze, the characters can reach the area of the Citadel where Szass Tam weaves his ritual. (See "Next Steps" when the characters descend into these tunnels.)

C14: Family Lounge

This rich-looking lounge contains plush crimson armchairs gathered around a central table.

Members of the family relax and eat their meals in this lounge.

C15: Tower Summit

Szass Tam's forces have created this illusion of Zulkir Thrul in danger.

When the characters come within 10 feet of the outside of this tower on foot or via flight, read or paraphrase the following:

A massive, four-horned fiend leaps onto the top of the tower, laughing hideously. It is joined by a flying mage with red robes and facial tattoos and by a skull alight with green flames, which flies at you, screaming, "You shall pay with your lives for opposing Szass Tam!"

The skull is Yoreth (Demilich), and the mage is the Red Wizard Jarek (Medium Archmage). They are further described in "Lich's Strike Force." Accompanying them is a Balor that slipped onto the Material Plane near the castle. Yoreth and Jarek enticed the fiendish general to assault the castle, promising the balor could kill powerful heroes—the characters. These three fight the characters to the death.

title: Chapter 7: Szass Tam Must Die
html:
Chapter 7: Szass Tam Must Die

Fight Szass Tam and save Thay from destruction.

  • Adventure for Level 19 Characters
  • Sessions 2
Szass Tam nears the end of his ritual to raise an overwhelming horde of malefites.

Key Plot Points

The following information is key to this chapter's story:

  • Sarrukh Guardians. Magical serpentine creatures called sarrukhs guard the entrance to Szass Tam's ritual chamber. The characters must circumvent or dispatch the sarrukhs before they face the lich.
  • Stop Szass Tam. When the characters arrive in the ritual chamber, they can confront Szass Tam and his allies and stop him from raising a malefite army that will destroy Thay.

Preparation

Before running this chapter, prepare as follows:

  • Step 1. Read the "Running This Chapter" section, including "Character Advancement."
  • Step 2. Familiarize yourself with the Key NPCs table below.
  • Step 3. Bookmark the stat blocks below, which appear in the Monster Manual and on D&D Beyond unless otherwise noted. If a stat block appears in appendix B, an asterisk appears after its name:
  • Arisen Sarrukh*
  • Dracolich
  • Nalfeshnee
  • Sarrukh Tyrant*
  • Szass Tam*
  • Vampire Umbral Lord
  • Xelnene Thrul
Key NPCs
NameRoleStat BlockLocation
DrevoralyxDraconic malefite allied with Szass TamDracolich (Huge)Z13
Nara CrocusSzass Tam's lieutenantVampire Umbral Lord (Medium)Z14
Szass TamLich plotting to unleash a malefite horde against ThaySee appendix BZ14
VartheethSarrukh who might surrenderSarrukh Tyrant (see appendix B)Z2
Vorsoth and XileeshSarrukh clan leaders and Szass Tam's alliesArisen Sarrukh (see appendix B)Z13
Xelnene ThrulHuman zulkir of evocation and Operation Deadfall's leaderSee appendix BZ14

Running This Chapter

This chapter takes place after the characters have found the tunnel from Castle Thrul to the Citadel.

Character Advancement

The characters should be level 19 when this chapter begins. They should be level 20 by the time they face Szass Tam in area Z14.

Reaching the Citadel

The tunnel in Castle Thrul leads to a labyrinthine underground structure of caverns and passageways. The route to the Citadel is about two miles.

These underground areas, which are in Darkness, are difficult to navigate. To keep the characters on the safest, most direct route, one character makes a 15 Wisdom (Survival) check. On a success, the characters reach the sanctum without incident. Proceed with "Szass Tam's Sanctum."

On a failure, the characters stray into dangerous tunnels and encounter monsters, as described below.

Underground Ambush

Use any area on the Underdark Warren map in the Dungeon Master's Guide for this encounter.

Read or paraphrase the following, which assumes the characters have a way to see in the dark:

Three hulking serpentine warriors wielding polearms patrol this passage.

These three Sarrukh Tyrant serve Szass Tam and search the area for intruders.

When the sarrukhs notice the characters, read or paraphrase the following:

One of the serpentine horrors shrieks in Common, "Intruders! For nearing the sarrukh stronghold, you shall die. For defying Szass Tam, you shall become the lich's rotting puppets!"

Sarrukh Lore

A character can take the Study action and make a 15 Intelligence (History) check. On a success, the character realizes the creatures are sarrukhs and recalls that these creatures once commanded a wicked empire that spanned Faerûn, but it fell millennia ago. The character knows sarrukhs are now nearly extinct.

The sarrukhs fight to the death. Once the characters defeat the sarrukhs, they can proceed to the Citadel, emerging in Szass Tam's sanctum.

Szass Tam's Sanctum

A subterranean level of the Citadel serves as Szass Tam's sanctum for weaving the Malefice Mortum ritual.

Like the rest of the Citadel, the sarrukhs built this area millennia ago. Szass Tam long ago allied with the sarrukhs still in this complex. He promised that once he controls Thay, he'll help them conquer the other peoples in the Underdark under Thaymount.

Sanctum Features

Szass Tam's sanctum has the following features.

Ceilings

Ceilings in the sanctum are 40 feet high, with the exception of areas Z13 and Z14. Ceilings in those areas are 100 feet high.

Doors

The sanctum's doors are made of stone. All are unlocked except the double door to the hall of corrupted lava (area Z13), which is locked with an Arcane Lock spell. (See "Doors" in the Dungeon Master's Guide.)

Lighting

Sconces and braziers with Continual Flame spells cast on them illuminate the sanctum with green-tinted Dim Light. The exception is area Z13, where the green lava's glow creates eerie Bright Light.

Szass Tam's Lair

The sanctum is Szass Tam's lair. It exhibits the effects described in his entry in appendix B.

Unhallowed Ward

Szass Tam's evil magic has created a permanent effect similar to that of a Hallow spell, but it affects the whole sanctum. Celestials can't willingly enter the sanctum, and Humanoids have Vulnerability to Necrotic damage here. The effect is suppressed for any creature in the area of an Antimagic Field spell. The effect can't be dispelled.

Sanctum Locations

The following locations are keyed to map 7.1.

Z1: Entryway

An ancient statue of a serpentine warrior wielding a polearm stands against the far wall. Green light flickers off its carved armor and scales.

The statue depicts a hero of the long-lost sarrukh empire. A character can take the Study action to examine the statue and make a 15 Intelligence (History) check. On a success, the character recalls the lore about sarrukhs described in "Underground Ambush."

Poisoned Dart Traps

The traps marked by the letter T on the map are poisoned dart traps, as described in the Poisoned Darts, except the darts—sarrukh fangs dripping with poison—deal 24 (7d6) Poison damage each.

Z2: Communal Hall

Two serpentine figures near a long table argue in a hissing, guttural tongue. Both have the heads and lower bodies of snakes but torsos like those of humanoids, albeit scaly. One is bulkier than the other and has glowing green eyes; black rot mottles its desiccated scales.

The bulky creature is Ssarthe (Arisen Sarrukh), who achieved undeath long ago. Ssarthe argues in Draconic with Vartheeth (Sarrukh Tyrant).

The sarrukhs fight the characters on noticing them. Ssarthe fights to the death, but if Ssarthe is killed or Vartheeth is Bloodied, Vartheeth surrenders. Vartheeth reveals the following if the characters agree to let her flee:

  • Return to Glory. Szass Tam has promised this sarrukh clan he'll help them conquer the other peoples under Thaymount once his ritual is complete. Vartheeth is skeptical, as the lich ignored their earlier requests for such help for centuries.
  • Ritual Chamber Guardians. An undead dragon with glowing green eyes guards the lich's ritual chamber. The dragon is joined by undead sarrukhs named Vorsoth and Xileesh, the stronghold's leaders, whom the lich has promised to install as emperors in the future sarrukh empire. Szass Tam has also promised the dragon something valuable in exchange for his service, but Vartheeth doesn't know the details. Vartheeth suspects Szass Tam is lying about everything.
  • Sarrukh Superiority. Like all sarrukhs, Vartheeth believes sarrukhs are superior to everyone else.
  • Undead Aspirations. Like most sarrukhs, Vartheeth wants to become undead to ensure she'll witness the resurgence of the sarrukh empire.

Z3: Hall of Tyranny

Flickering green light from sconces forms shadowy scenes on the walls of serpentine creatures hoisting polearms. An overwhelming sense of dread fills you as the shadows leap from the walls and slither toward you.

This magical effect is an illusion.

Illusory Danger

When a character enters this area, they can take the Study action and make a 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to try to recognize the illusion.

On a failed check, a character makes a 15 Wisdom saving throw, taking 42 (12d6) Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

A character is subject to this magical effect only once. A character who carries a figurine from area Z9 is immune to this effect.

Z4: Library

Bookcases filled with weathered tomes surround a reading table here. Two bulky serpentine figures peruse the volumes on the shelves.

Two Arisen Sarrukh (see appendix B) search through these books about necromancy, seeking to better understand Szass Tam's ritual. The sarrukhs fight the characters on noticing them.

Treasure

The books contain all the Necromancy spells in the Player's Handbook. A character can take the Search action and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to examine the books. On a success, the character finds five tomes worth 500 GP each.

Z5: South Sarrukh Chambers

A wall divides this hall into two chambers with a doorless opening between them. Each chamber holds a nest of green cushions; the northern chamber also holds a desk.

The clan's sarrukh tyrants rest here and in area Z6.

In the northern chamber, an unlocked drawer in the northwest desk holds a Potion of Vitality. In the southern chamber, underneath the cushions is a small pouch containing 100 PP.

Z6: North Sarrukh Quarters

Several nests made from blankets lie to the north.

If the characters spend 10 minutes searching the northwest nest, they find Vartheeth's journal, written in Draconic. It reveals the information she might mention in area Z2.

Z7: Magical Laboratory

A twenty-foot-wide rune scribed on the floor glows green. Two serpentine figures chant incantations in a hissing, guttural tone, their eyes closed in concentration. Tables holding open books and vials of liquid sit along the walls.

The chanting figures are Tresshe and Yethel (Sarrukh Tyrant; see appendix B). They know Szass Tam's ritual has bathed the area in unholy magic (see "Unhallowed Ward"). They hope the effect, mixed with their own magic, will turn them undead.

The sarrukhs fight the characters on sight but surrender if Bloodied. In exchange for being allowed to escape, they reveal the information Vartheeth might share in area Z2, though they believe Szass Tam's promise.

Glowing Rune

The rune on the floor thrums with ancient magic. As an action, a creature can stand on the rune and feel magical energy flow through them. For the next hour, whenever that creature casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, one target of the spellcaster's choice has Disadvantage on saves against the spell.

Treasure

A Potion of Supreme Healing lies on the northeast table.

Z8: Scriptorium

The tables here bear writing supplies and coins. Three serpentine figures are writing furiously.

In this scriptorium, three Sarrukh Tyrant (see appendix B) scribe Spell Scroll to help Szass Tam's cause. They fight the characters on noticing them.

Treasure

The tables hold three sets of Calligrapher's Supplies, as well as Ink and Parchment. The tables also contain three Spell Scroll of Delayed Blast Fireball, a Spell Scroll of Imprisonment, and a Spell Scroll of Time Stop.

The coins on the tables amount to 1,000 GP total.

Z9: Shrine

Candles burn green here in a semicircle on the floor, and foot-tall serpentine figurines stand on velvet cloths. The east wall is carved with a relief of an enormous serpent biting its own tail.

This is a shrine to the enigmatic World Serpent and other gods the sarrukhs venerate. Characters proficient in Religion identify the World Serpent carving.

Figurines

The figurines on the ground depict snakelike or draconic deities that the sarrukhs believe are manifestations of the World Serpent. Characters proficient in Religion identify the figurines as depicting the following deities:

  • Asgorath:. Dragon said to have created the world
  • Jazirian:. Couatl deity
  • Shekinester:. Patron god of nagas

There is one figurine per character; more than one figurine can depict each deity if needed.

Development

A character carrying a figurine is immune to the effects of the illusion in area Z3.

Z10: Storage

This room bears trunks and crates.

These trunks contain 50 Rations total.

Z11: Hall of Glories

Dotting this corridor are frescoes and statues depicting serpentine conquerers cowing myriad other creatures depicted as terrified and weak.

Characters proficient in History recognize that the frescoes and statues depict sarrukh history.

Z12: Antechamber of Skulls

Heroes prepare to confront the sarrukhs who guard an antechamber in Szass Tam's sanctum.

Two curved stairways rise five feet to a double door guarded by two serpentine warriors, one wielding a fauchard and the other a trident.

The guards are an Arisen Sarrukh and Sarrukh Tyrant (see appendix B for both), who fight the characters on noticing them.

Explosive Glyph

A nearly imperceptible glyph is scribed on the center of the double door (see area Z13). Noticing the glyph requires a successful 21 Wisdom (Perception) check.

The glyph triggers when a creature touches the double door. When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 30-foot Cone [Area of Effect] originating from the center of the door. Each creature in that area makes a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 22 (5d8) Acid damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Z13: Hall of Corrupted Lava

The double door to this area is locked with an Arcane Lock spell. When the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

Heat rises off the green river of bubbling lava that snakes northward toward a dais, where an enormous dragon of bone and desiccated flesh looms. Two serpentine warriors with rotting scales, each brandishing a trident, stand near the dais. Rubble chokes alcoves to the east and west.

The dragon is Drevoralyx, a Huge Dracolich. Two Arisen Sarrukh (see appendix B) accompany him—Vorsoth and Xileesh, the sarrukh clan's leaders. Since Drevoralyx isn't a true dracolich, he has no lair (see "Draconic Malefite").

When any of these creatures notice the characters, read or paraphrase the following:

The dragon shouts in a guttural voice, "You must be the maggots Szass Tam described. Leave now, or I shall squash you like the bugs you are!"

The creatures will entertain a question before they fight the characters to the death. If the characters ask why they're protecting Szass Tam, Drevoralyx reveals that Szass Tam has promised to install him as the malefites' general. Vorsoth and Xileesh reveal that Szass Tam has promised to help them become joint emperors of a new sarrukh empire in the Underdark.

Draconic Malefite

A character can take the Study action to examine Drevoralyx and make a 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a success, the character realizes the foul magic from Szass Tam's ritual animated the dead dragon, who traveled here from another part of the Citadel. The character knows this means Drevoralyx has no lair, doesn't have the Soul Gem trait, and is destroyed when reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Alcoves

The alcoves are blocked with rubble from collapsed stairs. Szass Tam blocked these stairways to ensure no one could enter his sanctum from here.

Lava River

The lava flow here occurs naturally, fueled by a nearby volcano. Szass Tam's magic has corrupted it, turning it green. The lava is 5 feet deep and Difficult Terrain. A creature that enters the lava or begins its turn there takes 27 (5d10) Fire damage and 27 (5d10) Necrotic damage.

Z14: Ritual Chamber

If the characters failed to receive the help of the pirates in chapter 5, Szass Tam received a number of ritual-boosting demon skulls equal to the number of characters. Add the following to the description of the ritual chamber after the first paragraph:

The horned, fanged skulls of fiends rest along the ritual circle. Runes glowing with green light cover the skulls.

When the characters enter this chamber, read or paraphrase the following:

A wide circle inscribed with profane runes glows green on this chamber's floor. Around the circle, shimmering images of hulking fiends bend backward unnaturally. A corona of green energy flows from the fiends to Szass Tam, who floats high above the ground, clutching a blackened spellbook.

In the southwest corner, Zulkir Thrul stands unmoving with a look of horror frozen on her face. Nearby, a pale woman's hands pulse with shadowy magic, and two enormous boar-headed beasts slaver.

Szass Tam smiles. "Ah, maggots," he sneers. "You must truly wish to be crushed. You think yourselves bold, but you are simply this generation's sad excuse for those who futilely stand against me."

The zulkir of necromancy beckons you with a clawlike hand. "Come, rail and rant as you must. Then die and be reborn as I please!"

Szass Tam (see appendix B) flies 50 feet above the chamber's floor. He's defended by the vampire Nara Crocus (Medium Vampire Umbral Lord), whose lair is elsewhere in the Citadel, and by her two Nalfeshnee bodyguards.

Szass Tam

When this combat begins, the lich is maintaining Concentration on his ritual. If he's reduced to 250 Hit Points or fewer, he stops concentrating on the ritual if his Concentration is still unbroken. Szass Tam keeps his distance from the characters while his allies are alive and uses every Action, Reaction, and Legendary Action at his disposal.

Zulkir Thrul

Under the effects of Power Word Stun, Xelnene Thrul (see appendix B) has the Stunned condition and 1 Hit Points remaining. Roll Initiative for Thrul. At the end of each of her turns, roll a 21 Constitution saving throw for Thrul as she tries to shake off the spell. On a success, she no longer has the Stunned condition and joins the combat against the lich. Szass Tam targets her on his next turn.

Ritual Skulls

If present, the skulls discharge magical bolts that target the characters.

Every round on Initiative count 0 (losing ties), each skull targets a random player character. The character makes a 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

Demon Conduits

Szass Tam is channeling necromantic magic through a translucent glabrezu, goristro, marilith, and nalfeshnee. The demons' souls are split between the Material Plane and the Abyss; if Szass Tam is killed or stops concentrating, these demons return to the Abyss.

Spirit-Binding Censer

If the characters retrieved the Spirit-Binding Censer (see appendix A) from the temple of the Red Knight in chapter 4, they can use it to trap Szass Tam's soul for a hundred years.

Development

If Szass Tam dies, a flash of golden light bathes the sanctum in virtuous energy. All evidence of the lich's ritual disappears. Further, the holy energy replaces Szass Tam's blackened spellbook with the Book of Exalted Deeds, which lies closed in the center of the chamber.

Conclusion

The outcome of the final battle has significant ramifications for Thay.

Success

If the characters disrupt Szass Tam's ritual, they foil his plans. Red Wizards, perhaps with the characters' help, eventually defeat the malefites and demons that have attacked the nation. If the characters kill Szass Tam but don't have the censer, Szass Tam revives in 1d10 days with all his Hit Points in another part of the Citadel. Thay must contend with the enraged lich, though he won't try anything as dramatic as this for several years.

If the characters trap Szass Tam's soul in the censer, Thay has a century to fortify itself against the lich and reshape its future.

Zulkir Thrul

If Thrul survives (or if the characters raise her from the dead), read or paraphrase the following:

After a moment spent breathing deeply and smoothing her robes, Zulkir Thrul turns to you.

"Operatives—friends—you did it. You stopped Szass Tam. More importantly, you saved Thay."

A small smile crosses her face. "It's time for me to return to Eltabbar. Won't you join me, heroes? We must discuss your reward."

After they return to Eltabbar, Thrul awards each character any Legendary magic item they request. She invites the heroes to work with her to fight for a better Thay for as long as they are willing.

New Zulkir of Necromancy

If any character is a Wizard with the Necromancer subclass or can prove their proficiency at Necromancy, Thrul suggests they vie to replace Szass Tam as zulkir of necromancy. This could be a satisfying capstone to the character's adventuring career. In this case, Thrul convinces the other zulkirs that the character earned the position by helping defeat Szass Tam. The characters have an opportunity to bring political change to Thay. They might need to contend with the lich's return, but that's a later adventure.

The Mavericks

If the characters visit the dissident Red Wizards after defeating Szass Tam, the mages express their gratitude for saving Thay—in their own self-aggrandizing way—and Sabinia thanks them for saving her sister. Each mage extends a standing invitation to the characters to visit their many estates.

Failure

If the party fails to disrupt Szass Tam's ritual, their mission fails, and Szass Tam's army of malefites kills thousands. The other zulkirs are killed or driven into hiding. Szass Tam's forces hunt down the Mavericks and slay them. The lich declares himself regent. He then turns his sights to conquering neighboring Aglarond and Rashemen.

If they survive, the characters must flee Thay. They might later become generals in a force that opposes the malefites. They will need to confront Szass Tam's malefite leaders and sycophants before they can hope to weaken the lich's grip on the nation.

title: Szass Tam nears the end of his ritual to raise an overwhelming horde of malefites.
Key Plot Points
html:
Key Plot Points

The following information is key to this chapter's story:

  • Sarrukh Guardians. Magical serpentine creatures called sarrukhs guard the entrance to Szass Tam's ritual chamber. The characters must circumvent or dispatch the sarrukhs before they face the lich.
  • Stop Szass Tam. When the characters arrive in the ritual chamber, they can confront Szass Tam and his allies and stop him from raising a malefite army that will destroy Thay.

title: Preparation
html:
Preparation

Before running this chapter, prepare as follows:

  • Step 1. Read the "Running This Chapter" section, including "Character Advancement."
  • Step 2. Familiarize yourself with the Key NPCs table below.
  • Step 3. Bookmark the stat blocks below, which appear in the Monster Manual and on D&D Beyond unless otherwise noted. If a stat block appears in appendix B, an asterisk appears after its name:
  • Arisen Sarrukh*
  • Dracolich
  • Nalfeshnee
  • Sarrukh Tyrant*
  • Szass Tam*
  • Vampire Umbral Lord
  • Xelnene Thrul

This is a shrine to the enigmatic World Serpent and other gods the sarrukhs venerate. Characters proficient in Religion identify the World Serpent carving.

Figurines

The figurines on the ground depict snakelike or draconic deities that the sarrukhs believe are manifestations of the World Serpent. Characters proficient in Religion identify the figurines as depicting the following deities:

  • Asgorath:. Dragon said to have created the world
  • Jazirian:. Couatl deity
  • Shekinester:. Patron god of nagas

There is one figurine per character; more than one figurine can depict each deity if needed.

Development

A character carrying a figurine is immune to the effects of the illusion in area Z3.

Z10: Storage

This room bears trunks and crates.

These trunks contain 50 Rations total.

Z11: Hall of Glories

Dotting this corridor are frescoes and statues depicting serpentine conquerers cowing myriad other creatures depicted as terrified and weak.

Characters proficient in History recognize that the frescoes and statues depict sarrukh history.

Z12: Antechamber of Skulls

Heroes prepare to confront the sarrukhs who guard an antechamber in Szass Tam's sanctum.

Two curved stairways rise five feet to a double door guarded by two serpentine warriors, one wielding a fauchard and the other a trident.

The guards are an Arisen Sarrukh and Sarrukh Tyrant (see appendix B for both), who fight the characters on noticing them.

Explosive Glyph

A nearly imperceptible glyph is scribed on the center of the double door (see area Z13). Noticing the glyph requires a successful 21 Wisdom (Perception) check.

The glyph triggers when a creature touches the double door. When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 30-foot Cone [Area of Effect] originating from the center of the door. Each creature in that area makes a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 22 (5d8) Acid damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Z13: Hall of Corrupted Lava

The double door to this area is locked with an Arcane Lock spell. When the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

Heat rises off the green river of bubbling lava that snakes northward toward a dais, where an enormous dragon of bone and desiccated flesh looms. Two serpentine warriors with rotting scales, each brandishing a trident, stand near the dais. Rubble chokes alcoves to the east and west.

The dragon is Drevoralyx, a Huge Dracolich. Two Arisen Sarrukh (see appendix B) accompany him—Vorsoth and Xileesh, the sarrukh clan's leaders. Since Drevoralyx isn't a true dracolich, he has no lair (see "Draconic Malefite").

When any of these creatures notice the characters, read or paraphrase the following:

The dragon shouts in a guttural voice, "You must be the maggots Szass Tam described. Leave now, or I shall squash you like the bugs you are!"

The creatures will entertain a question before they fight the characters to the death. If the characters ask why they're protecting Szass Tam, Drevoralyx reveals that Szass Tam has promised to install him as the malefites' general. Vorsoth and Xileesh reveal that Szass Tam has promised to help them become joint emperors of a new sarrukh empire in the Underdark.

Draconic Malefite

A character can take the Study action to examine Drevoralyx and make a 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a success, the character realizes the foul magic from Szass Tam's ritual animated the dead dragon, who traveled here from another part of the Citadel. The character knows this means Drevoralyx has no lair, doesn't have the Soul Gem trait, and is destroyed when reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Alcoves

The alcoves are blocked with rubble from collapsed stairs. Szass Tam blocked these stairways to ensure no one could enter his sanctum from here.

Lava River

The lava flow here occurs naturally, fueled by a nearby volcano. Szass Tam's magic has corrupted it, turning it green. The lava is 5 feet deep and Difficult Terrain. A creature that enters the lava or begins its turn there takes 27 (5d10) Fire damage and 27 (5d10) Necrotic damage.

Z14: Ritual Chamber

If the characters failed to receive the help of the pirates in chapter 5, Szass Tam received a number of ritual-boosting demon skulls equal to the number of characters. Add the following to the description of the ritual chamber after the first paragraph:

The horned, fanged skulls of fiends rest along the ritual circle. Runes glowing with green light cover the skulls.

When the characters enter this chamber, read or paraphrase the following:

A wide circle inscribed with profane runes glows green on this chamber's floor. Around the circle, shimmering images of hulking fiends bend backward unnaturally. A corona of green energy flows from the fiends to Szass Tam, who floats high above the ground, clutching a blackened spellbook.

In the southwest corner, Zulkir Thrul stands unmoving with a look of horror frozen on her face. Nearby, a pale woman's hands pulse with shadowy magic, and two enormous boar-headed beasts slaver.

Szass Tam smiles. "Ah, maggots," he sneers. "You must truly wish to be crushed. You think yourselves bold, but you are simply this generation's sad excuse for those who futilely stand against me."

The zulkir of necromancy beckons you with a clawlike hand. "Come, rail and rant as you must. Then die and be reborn as I please!"

Szass Tam (see appendix B) flies 50 feet above the chamber's floor. He's defended by the vampire Nara Crocus (Medium Vampire Umbral Lord), whose lair is elsewhere in the Citadel, and by her two Nalfeshnee bodyguards.

Szass Tam

When this combat begins, the lich is maintaining Concentration on his ritual. If he's reduced to 250 Hit Points or fewer, he stops concentrating on the ritual if his Concentration is still unbroken. Szass Tam keeps his distance from the characters while his allies are alive and uses every Action, Reaction, and Legendary Action at his disposal.

Zulkir Thrul

Under the effects of Power Word Stun, Xelnene Thrul (see appendix B) has the Stunned condition and 1 Hit Points remaining. Roll Initiative for Thrul. At the end of each of her turns, roll a 21 Constitution saving throw for Thrul as she tries to shake off the spell. On a success, she no longer has the Stunned condition and joins the combat against the lich. Szass Tam targets her on his next turn.

Ritual Skulls

If present, the skulls discharge magical bolts that target the characters.

Every round on Initiative count 0 (losing ties), each skull targets a random player character. The character makes a 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

Demon Conduits

Szass Tam is channeling necromantic magic through a translucent glabrezu, goristro, marilith, and nalfeshnee. The demons' souls are split between the Material Plane and the Abyss; if Szass Tam is killed or stops concentrating, these demons return to the Abyss.

Spirit-Binding Censer

If the characters retrieved the Spirit-Binding Censer (see appendix A) from the temple of the Red Knight in chapter 4, they can use it to trap Szass Tam's soul for a hundred years.

Development

If Szass Tam dies, a flash of golden light bathes the sanctum in virtuous energy. All evidence of the lich's ritual disappears. Further, the holy energy replaces Szass Tam's blackened spellbook with the Book of Exalted Deeds, which lies closed in the center of the chamber.

title: Conclusion
html:
Conclusion

The outcome of the final battle has significant ramifications for Thay.

Success

If the characters disrupt Szass Tam's ritual, they foil his plans. Red Wizards, perhaps with the characters' help, eventually defeat the malefites and demons that have attacked the nation. If the characters kill Szass Tam but don't have the censer, Szass Tam revives in 1d10 days with all his Hit Points in another part of the Citadel. Thay must contend with the enraged lich, though he won't try anything as dramatic as this for several years.

If the characters trap Szass Tam's soul in the censer, Thay has a century to fortify itself against the lich and reshape its future.

Zulkir Thrul

If Thrul survives (or if the characters raise her from the dead), read or paraphrase the following:

After a moment spent breathing deeply and smoothing her robes, Zulkir Thrul turns to you.

"Operatives—friends—you did it. You stopped Szass Tam. More importantly, you saved Thay."

A small smile crosses her face. "It's time for me to return to Eltabbar. Won't you join me, heroes? We must discuss your reward."

After they return to Eltabbar, Thrul awards each character any Legendary magic item they request. She invites the heroes to work with her to fight for a better Thay for as long as they are willing.

New Zulkir of Necromancy

If any character is a Wizard with the Necromancer subclass or can prove their proficiency at Necromancy, Thrul suggests they vie to replace Szass Tam as zulkir of necromancy. This could be a satisfying capstone to the character's adventuring career. In this case, Thrul convinces the other zulkirs that the character earned the position by helping defeat Szass Tam. The characters have an opportunity to bring political change to Thay. They might need to contend with the lich's return, but that's a later adventure.

The Mavericks

If the characters visit the dissident Red Wizards after defeating Szass Tam, the mages express their gratitude for saving Thay—in their own self-aggrandizing way—and Sabinia thanks them for saving her sister. Each mage extends a standing invitation to the characters to visit their many estates.

Failure

If the party fails to disrupt Szass Tam's ritual, their mission fails, and Szass Tam's army of malefites kills thousands. The other zulkirs are killed or driven into hiding. Szass Tam's forces hunt down the Mavericks and slay them. The lich declares himself regent. He then turns his sights to conquering neighboring Aglarond and Rashemen.

If they survive, the characters must flee Thay. They might later become generals in a force that opposes the malefites. They will need to confront Szass Tam's malefite leaders and sycophants before they can hope to weaken the lich's grip on the nation.
